# RigSignal 0.3.3 test manifest

**CHRONO_SESSION:** `2026-08-04-rigsignal-033`  
**Frozen input:** `SPEC-DRAFT-2.md` (digest is the one pinned by `OVERSEER-RULING-20260804.md`; do not edit that file).  
**Fixture convention:** every transaction fixture uses the current 0.3.3 archive and a protected canonical state home unless the test says otherwise.  All 66 ordinary targets are semantically exact except targets named in the test. `N` means no primary record. `I[o,p,m]` is an exact-bound, schema-v2 protected `installing` record with obligations `o`, progress `p`, and `possible_mutation=m`; `S[o]` is an exact-bound, protected `installed` v2 record retaining completed obligations `o`. `P` is the complete validated installed predecessor. `M` is the 67th Step-11 bundle-meta target. A write count counts remote mutations only, not GET/resolve calls or local atomic replacements. “Fresh run” means a new process after the lock is released.

## Record schema and validator

### Schema-v2 wire grammar (normative test fixture)

The protected file bytes must equal RFC 8785 JCS serialization of one of the two
objects below: UTF-8, no duplicate members, no insignificant whitespace, and
object members sorted by JCS UTF-16 code-unit order. Arrays are in the listed
order; no validator may sort them before checking the stored bytes. Literals:
`sha256 := [0-9a-f]{64}`; `source_commit := [0-9a-f]{40}`;
`cluster_uuid := [A-Za-z0-9_-]{22}`;
`transaction_id := [0-9a-f]{8}-[0-9a-f]{4}-4[0-9a-f]{3}-[89ab][0-9a-f]{3}-[0-9a-f]{12}`;
`rfc3339_utc := [0-9]{4}-(0[1-9]|1[0-2])-(0[1-9]|[12][0-9]|3[01])T([01][0-9]|2[0-3]):[0-5][0-9]:[0-5][0-9](\\.[0-9]{1,9})?Z`.
`target_key := "es/" es_kind "/" target_name | "kibana/" space "/" so_type "/" so_id`, where
`es_kind := component-template|index-template|ingest-pipeline|security-role|transform|bundle-meta`,
`target_name`, `space`, `so_type`, and `so_id` are nonempty RFC 3986 percent-encoded UTF-8 segments (`(?:[A-Za-z0-9._~-]|%[0-9A-F]{2})+`); lowercase hex escapes and raw `/` are invalid. A saved-object mapping is exactly `{"destination_key":target_key,"submitted_key":target_key}`; its keys and values must be distinct only where the server supplied a remap. `progress` is an object keyed by each required `target_key`, with value exactly `planned`, `write-issued`, or `verified`.

The common member set is exactly `asset_set_sha256`, `bundle_sha256`, `bundle_version`,
`cluster_uuid`, `kibana_target`, `ownership_profile`, `schema_version`, `source_commit`,
`state`, and `targets`. `schema_version` is integer `2`; `ownership_profile` is
`"default"`; `bundle_version` is `"0.3.3"`; `kibana_target` is exactly
`{"origin":"https://<canonical-host>[:port]","spaces":["default","rigsignal"]}`;
and `targets` is an ascending bytewise-UTF-8 list of exactly 66
`{"digest":sha256,"key":target_key}` objects. The `installing` schema has, and only
has in addition, `caller_obligations`, `created_at`, `possible_mutation`,
`predecessor`, `progress`, and `transaction_id`; `created_at` matches `rfc3339_utc`,
`caller_obligations` is exactly `["assets-66"]` or
`["assets-66","full-flow-step-11"]`, and `predecessor` is either `null` or the
complete installed schema below. The `installed` schema has, and only has in
addition, `completed_at`, `completed_transaction_id`, and
`verified_target_set_sha256`; `completed_at` matches `rfc3339_utc`, and has neither
`progress`, `possible_mutation`, nor `predecessor`. The predecessor key set is
therefore exactly the common set plus those three installed-only keys; it must itself
be JCS-canonical and bind the same common immutable values.

### T-REC-1 — reject noncanonical v2 shape

**Source:** Sol2-#11, Sol2-#12.  
**Given:** `I[{assets-66},{all 66:verified},false]` altered in one parameterized case each: an unknown/missing schema key; duplicate JSON/progress key; non-JCS member order; unsorted target key; failure of one literal grammar above (including non-UTC/offset/invalid-date timestamp); target digest mismatch; or cardinality other than 66.  
**When:** assets-only performs its locked authoritative-record read.  
**Then:** engine exit `3`; durable record remains byte-identical malformed input (no replacement); remote writes `0`; fresh run again exits `3` until an operator repairs the local protected record.

### T-REC-2 — validate complete obligation and progress vocabulary

**Source:** Sol2-#3, Sol2-#6.  
**Given:** an otherwise exact `I` whose `caller_obligations` is any set other than `{assets-66}` or `{assets-66,full-flow-step-11}`, whose `M` progress is present without the latter obligation, whose latter obligation lacks exactly one `M` progress entry, or whose progress state is outside `planned|write-issued|verified`.  
**When:** either caller reads the record under the lock.  
**Then:** exit `3`; durable record unchanged; remote writes `0`; fresh run refuses identically.

### T-REC-3 — validate destination mapping and predecessor shape

**Source:** Sol2-#6, Sol2-#8.  
**Given:** `I[{assets-66},{so(tag,rigsignal,a):verified},false]` containing a mapping whose `submitted_key` is absent from `targets`, whose submitted/destination value fails `target_key`, duplicate `submitted_key`, a mapping member set other than the literal two-member grammar, or a predecessor whose key set/value/JCS bytes are not one complete strict installed schema binding.  
**When:** a saved-object resumption begins.  
**Then:** exit `3`; record unchanged; remote writes `0`; fresh run refuses until local repair.

### T-REC-4 — installed state retains completed obligations

**Source:** Sol2-#2, Sol2-#3.  
**Given:** a successful full-flow fixture with `I[{assets-66,full-flow-step-11},{66+M:verified},true]` and all 67 live targets exact.  
**When:** promotion executes.  
**Then:** exit `0`; durable record is `S[{assets-66,full-flow-step-11}]`, including `completed_transaction_id`, `completed_at`, and the 67-target verified-set hash; remote writes `0`; fresh assets-only run exits `0` with `0` writes and fresh full-flow run verifies `M` without recreating it.

### T-REC-5 — exact target accounting

**Source:** OvsC, Sol2-#3, probe PROBE-8.  
**Given:** the release bundle’s 29 saved-object source rows and all expanded target inventory inputs.  
**When:** inventory construction runs, then full-flow atomically expands its obligation before Step 11.  
**Then:** test exit `0`; initial durable record has exactly 66 JCS-ordered target/digest entries and `I[{assets-66},...,false]`; the expanded record is exactly `I[{assets-66,full-flow-step-11},{66 ordinary progress entries,M:planned},false]`; `M` is the one additional entry and is included in the verified-set hash; remote writes `0`; next run constructs the same ordered inventory and digest.

### T-REC-6 — independent default bundle-meta JCS golden body

**Source:** Sol gate exact-change 5.  
**Given:** a checked-in literal fixture of the release inventory’s 66 ordered
`{"digest":sha256,"key":target_key}` values, fixed test stamp
`"managed_by":"rigsignal-asset-bundle"`, version, source commit, ownership profile,
and fixed RFC3339-UTC test timestamp.  
**When:** the test independently constructs the complete default-profile bundle-meta
object using only that literal fixture and RFC 8785 JCS (it must not import, call, mock,
or copy output from production `marker_body()`), serializes it, and hashes its UTF-8
bytes.  
**Then:** the literal JCS body and SHA-256 equal the checked-in golden exactly; it binds
all 66 identities and digests plus the RigSignal ownership stamp; deleting, reordering,
or changing any one identity/digest/stamp byte fails; remote writes `0`.

## Snapshot hash

### T-HASH-1 — hash the immutable full-byte snapshot

**Source:** Sol2-#5.  
**Given:** `N` and an archive containing valid tar bytes followed by a sentinel trailing byte sequence.  
**When:** the archive is opened once, copied to protected `0600` snapshot storage, fsynced, hashed from offset zero through EOF, and parsed from that snapshot.  
**Then:** exit `0`; durable record is `I[{assets-66},{all:planned},false]` with `bundle_sha256=sha256(full original bytes including sentinel)`; remote writes `0`; fresh run accepts only that exact digest.
**ERRATA-1:** T-HASH-1 controls D2 §3.1: the streaming-while-parsing alternative is void; the protected full-byte snapshot is mandatory.

### T-HASH-2 — source mutation cannot change parsed binding

**Source:** Sol2-#5.  
**Given:** `N`, an archive whose bytes are changed in place after snapshot fsync but before parse.  
**When:** initialization continues.  
**Then:** exit `0`; durable record binds the pre-mutation snapshot digest and targets; remote writes `0`; fresh run supplied the changed source exits `3` as non-exact, while the original bytes resume the record.

### T-HASH-3 — path swap cannot change parsed binding

**Source:** Sol2-#5, D2 §8.2.  
**Given:** `N` and pathname `bundle.tgz`; after the descriptor is opened, its pathname is atomically replaced by a different valid bundle.  
**When:** initialization parses and publishes intent.  
**Then:** exit `0`; record digest and target set are those of the opened snapshot only; remote writes `0`; fresh run with replacement bytes exits `3`, never resumes against a mixed digest.

### T-HASH-4 — snapshot crash points are recoverable

**Source:** Sol2-#4, Sol2 state-edge “archive snapshot”.  
**Given:** `N` and failure injection at snapshot temp creation, after copy before fsync, after fsync before parse, during parse, and cleanup; residue is separately owned regular `.rigsignal-*`, symlink, foreign-owned/non-regular, or an unsafe name.  
**When:** initialization raises at each point and a fresh run inspects residue.  
**Then:** each initial pre-intent failure exits `2`, remains `N`, and makes `0` remote writes; the owned regular case removes only that named residue then starts `I[...,planned,false]`, while each symlink/foreign/non-regular/unsafe-name case exits `3`, leaves the residue byte-identical, and makes `0` writes.

### T-HASH-5 — protected-temp residue is never a record

**Source:** Sol2-#4, D2 §3.5.  
**Given:** `I[{assets-66},{one target:write-issued},true]` plus an owned regular same-directory hidden temp left by SIGKILL; parameterize the issued target as exact and absent-with-proven-create-only.  
**When:** a fresh process resumes.  
**Then:** exact exits `0`, promotes `S[{assets-66}]`, and writes exactly `0`; absent exits `0`, promotes the same `S`, and writes exactly `1`; neither treats the temp as a record; each next run exits `0` with `0` writes.

## Lock

### T-LOCK-1 — canonical state-home serializes marker paths

**Source:** Sol2-#9, Sol2 state-edge “two friendly invocations”.  
**Given:** two friendly same-UID callers with different protected `--assets-marker` paths but the same canonical `XDG_STATE_HOME`; marker A has `I[{assets-66},{one:write-issued},true]` and holds the canonical state-home lock, marker B is `N`, and all remote targets are exact.  
**When:** second invocation starts before release.  
**Then:** second exits `3`; marker B remains `N` and it creates no competing record; remote writes `0`; after release, its fresh run creates and promotes its own `S[{assets-66}]` with `0` writes because all targets are exact.

### T-LOCK-2 — two-XDG-state-home bypass is documented, not claimed serialized

**Source:** owner ratification 3, Sol2-#9.  
**Given:** two friendly same-UID callers with distinct canonical state-home domains `A` and `B`, each with `N` in its own domain, the same remote target set, and one explicitly named guarded-class target absent while all other targets are exact.  
**When:** both invoke concurrently.  
**Then:** both engines exit `0` after one create-only success and one exact conflict reread; each durable state home contains only its own `S[{assets-66}]`; total remote writes are exactly `1` for the single absent target; each next run exits `0` with `0` writes. This test asserts the guarantee is limited to one canonical state-home domain.
**ERRATA-2:** T-LOCK-2 controls D2 §3.2’s “one user-global” wording: serialization is guaranteed only within a canonical state-home domain, not across caller-selected `XDG_STATE_HOME` values.

### T-LOCK-3 — no authoritative pre-lock read

**Source:** Sol2-#9, Sol1-#8.  
**Given:** a path-security-valid primary initially `S[{assets-66}]`; another process atomically replaces it with exact `I[{assets-66},{one:write-issued},true]` while the first waits for the lock.  
**When:** the first process acquires the lock.  
**Then:** it exits `0` only after acting from the new `I` and exact reread; durable record becomes `S[{assets-66}]`; remote writes `0`; next run is a zero-write success.

### T-LOCK-4 — lock acquisition boundary follows key recovery

**Source:** Sol2-#5, Sol2 state-edge “key mutation → held lock”.  
**Given:** incomplete enrollment performs exactly one persisted enrollment-key mutation, assets record `I[{assets-66},{all:planned},false]`, and another process holds the assets lock.  
**When:** recovery reaches lock acquisition.  
**Then:** exit `4` (the persisted possible-mutation state dominates); assets durable record remains unchanged; remote writes are exactly `1` enrollment write and `0` asset writes; fresh run reconciles enrollment then resumes the asset record under the lock.

## State machine and crash edges

### T-SM-1 — installed assets-only extends durably for full flow

**Source:** Sol2 state-edge “installed assets-only → full-flow”, Sol2-#2.  
**Given:** `S[{assets-66}]`, 66 exact targets, and absent `M`.  
**When:** full-flow starts and crashes immediately before or immediately after atomic replacement adding `full-flow-step-11`.  
**Then:** each SIGKILL subprocess return code is `-9`; before-replace crash leaves `S[{assets-66}]`, after-replace crash leaves `I[{assets-66,full-flow-step-11},{66:verified,M:planned},false]`; remote writes `0`; fresh full-flow rerun creates/verifies `M` once and promotes `S[{assets-66,full-flow-step-11}]`.

### T-SM-2 — installed full-flow remains valid for assets-only

**Source:** Sol2 state-edge “installed full-flow → assets-only”.  
**Given:** `S[{assets-66,full-flow-step-11}]` and all 67 targets exact.  
**When:** assets-only runs.  
**Then:** exit `0`; record remains that `S`; remote writes `0`; fresh full-flow run also exits `0` with `0` writes.

### T-SM-3 — ordinary missing target demotes installed atomically

**Source:** Sol2 state-edge “installed current → installing”.  
**Given:** `S[{assets-66}]` with exactly one ordinary target absent.  
**When:** assets-only classifies the absence.  
**Then:** exit `0`; durable record first becomes `I[{assets-66},{missing:write-issued,others:verified},true]` retaining exact predecessor `P`, then `S[{assets-66}]`; remote writes `1` create-only; next run exits `0` with `0` writes.

### T-SM-4 — crash during ordinary demotion

**Source:** Sol2 state-edge “crash during installed→installing demotion”.  
**Given:** the `S` and absent target from T-SM-3.  
**When:** SIGKILL occurs before replace, after replace before directory fsync, and after read-back.  
**Then:** each SIGKILL subprocess return code is `-9`; durable record is either old `S` or complete `I` with exact predecessor, never partial JSON; remote writes `0`; fresh run creates exactly once and promotes `S`.

### T-SM-5 — full-flow installing cannot be silently promoted by assets-only

**Source:** Sol2 state-edge “full-flow installing → assets-only new write”.  
**Given:** `I[{assets-66,full-flow-step-11},{one ordinary:planned,M:planned},false]`, ordinary target absent, and assets-only cannot execute Step 11.  
**When:** assets-only creates and verifies the ordinary target.  
**Then:** exit `4`; durable record is `I[{assets-66,full-flow-step-11},{ordinary:verified,M:planned},true]`; remote writes `1`; fresh assets-only exits `4` and preserves the record, while fresh full-flow writes/verifies `M` and promotes.

### T-SM-6 — zero-write cross-caller incomplete state remains exit 4

**Source:** owner ratification 2, Sol2 state-edge “same cross-caller zero writes”.  
**Given:** parameter cases `I[{assets-66,full-flow-step-11},{66:verified,M:planned},true]`, all 66 exact, assets-only cannot execute Step 11, and `M` is separately exact or absent-with-proven-create-only.  
**When:** assets-only runs without dispatching HTTP.  
**Then:** assets-only exits `4`, emits a redacted recovery token, preserves the record, and writes `0`; fresh full-flow exits `0` with `0` writes for exact `M` and exactly `1` for absent `M`, verifies it, and promotes.
**ERRATA-3:** T-SM-6 controls D2 §6 (especially lines 236 and 239): a persisted `possible_mutation` exits `4` until reconciliation, so the later-no-write exit-3 carve-out is void.

### T-SM-7 — destination mapping survives crash

**Source:** Sol2 state-edge “mapping learned → crash”, Sol2-#8.  
**Given:** `I[{assets-66},{SO submitted key:write-issued},true]`; the selected saved-object adapter has received a destination mapping for that key and the remote object is exact at that destination.  
**When:** crash injection fires before and after atomic persistence of the mapping.  
**Then:** before persistence, fresh run resolves submitted and destination identity before deciding; after persistence, fresh run uses the validated stored mapping; each fresh run exits `0`, record becomes `S[{assets-66}]`, remote writes `0`, and no duplicate physical object is created.

### T-SM-8 — final-GET-before-promotion crash repeats full verification

**Source:** Sol2-#4.  
**Given:** `I[{assets-66},{all 66:verified},true]` and all live targets exact.  
**When:** crash fires after the final target GET but before promotion begins.  
**Then:** SIGKILL subprocess return code is `-9`; record remains `I`; remote writes `0`; fresh run rereads all 66 targets, then promotes `S[{assets-66}]`; its next run is a zero-write exit `0`.

### T-SM-9 — write-issued before dispatch is uncertain

**Source:** Sol2 state-edge “write-issued but HTTP never started”.  
**Given:** `I[{assets-66},{one:planned},false]`; parameterize the target as still absent and now exact when the fresh process reads it.  
**When:** `write-issued=true` is fsynced and an injected exception occurs before HTTP dispatch.  
**Then:** injected exception exits `4`; record is `I[{assets-66},{one:write-issued},true]`; initial remote writes `0`; fresh-absent exits `0` after exactly `1` proven create-only write, while fresh-exact exits `0` after exactly `0`; each promotes only after full reconciliation.

### T-SM-10 — verified record cannot hide replacement before promotion

**Source:** Sol1-#9, Sol2-#12.  
**Given:** `I[{assets-66},{all:verified},true]`; parameterize flags `none`, `repair`, valid direction, and valid repair+direction; a foreign actor replaces one target after its verified GET and before final reverify.  
**When:** promotion reverify reaches that target.  
**Then:** current run exits `4`, record remains `I` with uncertainty, and writes `0`; fresh exact exits `0`/`0` writes, fresh unowned/Kibana/unreadable exits `4`/`0`, and fresh stamped ES writes exactly `1`/exits `0` only in a table-authorized repair or valid-direction row (otherwise `4`/`0`).

### T-SM-11 — repair and transition preserve predecessor

**Source:** Sol2 state-edge “each repair and version-transition demotion”.  
**Given:** exact transition parameters: (a) current `S[{assets-66}]` + stamped divergent ES + `--repair`; (b) prior `S` + valid upward predecessor/direction + `--upgrade`; (c) prior `S` + valid downward predecessor/direction + `--allow-downgrade`; and the invalid opposite-direction rows.  
**When:** the machine demotes to installing and crashes before/after replacement.  
**Then:** pre-replace leaves old `S`; post-replace leaves complete `I` containing byte-for-byte validated predecessor `P`; crash leg writes `0`. Fresh rows (a), (b), and (c) each issue exactly `1` qualified ES write then exit `0`/promote; opposite direction exits `2`/`0`; no row writes Kibana or unstamped ES.

### T-SM-12 — incomplete enrollment preserves each asset-record class

**Source:** Sol2 state-edge “key mutation → malformed/unavailable record”.  
**Given:** parameter cases after exactly one persisted enrollment-key mutation: valid `I`, malformed protected asset file, and unavailable exact bundle for `I`.  
**When:** key recovery then canonical binding succeeds and asset record handling runs.  
**Then:** all cases exit `4`; valid `I` remains unchanged, malformed file remains unchanged, unavailable `I` remains unchanged; remote writes exactly `1` enrollment and `0` assets; fresh run remains exit `4` until reconciliation/local repair, never downgrades to `2` or `3`.

## Reconciliation predicates and class compensations

### T-RECON-1 — marker-loss ES self-heal is available

**Source:** OvsA.  
**Given:** `N`, one ES target is semantically divergent but carries valid `managed_by=rigsignal-asset-bundle`, every Kibana target is exact, and all other ES targets are exact.  
**When:** assets-only runs with no flags.  
**Then:** exit `0`; record progresses through `I[{assets-66},{target:write-issued},true]` to `S[{assets-66}]`; remote writes exactly `1` authorized ES reconciliation; fresh run exits `0` with `0` writes.
**ERRATA-5:** T-RECON-1 controls D2 §5.3’s `none/installing + stamped divergent ES + no flags` refusal: marker loss permits this ES-only self-heal route after the complete Kibana fail-closed preflight in T-RECON-2.

### T-RECON-2 — marker-loss route remains fail-closed for Kibana

**Source:** OvsA, owner ratification 1.  
**Given:** parameterized first/middle/last inventory placement of one stamped divergent ES target and one present divergent Kibana target; a second parameter has the remaining Kibana targets split exact/absent.  
**When:** either caller runs.  
**Then:** every required Kibana classification completes before intent publication or any ES mutation; each permutation exits `3`, leaves durable `N`, makes `0` transport mutations, and leaves the ES target byte-identical. Absent Kibana targets may only exercise their proven create-only primitive when no divergent/unreadable Kibana target exists; any divergent/unreadable Kibana target blocks all writes. Fresh run refuses until owner remediation makes every Kibana target exact/deleted, after which T-RECON-1 may converge ES.

### T-RECON-3 — absent targets use proven conditional create per class

**Source:** probe CLASS-es-component-template, CLASS-es-index-template, CLASS-es-transform, CLASS-kibana-space, CLASS-kibana-security-role.  
**Given:** parameterized classes component template, index template, transform, Kibana space, and Kibana role with `I[{assets-66},{class target:planned},false]`, target absent, every other target exact.  
**When:** the class’s proven create primitive is dispatched on both 9.4.3 and 9.4.4.  
**Then:** exit `0`; record becomes `S[{assets-66}]`; remote writes exactly `1`; a repeat conditional create yields the probe-specific conflict (`400` for the three ES classes, `409` for Kibana space/role) followed by exact reread, and next installer run makes `0` writes.

### T-RECON-4 — guard-absent classes create only on a creation-confirmed clean path

**Source:** owner ratification 5 (2026-08-04), probe CLASS-es-ingest-pipeline, CLASS-es-security-role, `RESEARCH-CONDITIONAL-PRIMITIVES.md` TIMESTAMP-PROBE addendum (grade A).  
**Given:** separately for `es-ingest-pipeline` and `es-security-role`, `I[{assets-66},{target:planned},false]`, target GET-absent, every other target exact, and a unique ownership nonce for this one PUT (`_meta.controller_nonce` for a pipeline; `metadata.controller_nonce` for a role).  
**When:** the engine durably changes that target to `write-issued` with `possible_mutation=true`, issues exactly one PUT carrying the nonce, and performs the deterministic post-write creation check.  
**Then:** role requires response `role.created:true`; pipeline requires an exact nonce/body GET with `created_date_millis == modified_date_millis`. Only that creation-confirmed clean branch exits `0`, verifies, and promotes `S[{assets-66}]` after exactly `1` remote mutation. An overwrite-detector-positive branch is exclusively T-RECON-5/7: it exits `4`, retains `I[...,{target:write-issued},true]`, and cannot promote.

### T-RECON-5 — detected pipeline/role overwrite halts without restoration

**Source:** owner ratification 5 (2026-08-04), `RESEARCH-CONDITIONAL-PRIMITIVES.md` TIMESTAMP-PROBE addendum (grade A).  
**Given:** two deterministic race fixtures, each with the pre-PUT GET absent and all unrelated targets exact: (a) a foreign role is created after GET and before the nonce-bearing role PUT, so its PUT response is `role.created:false`; (b) a foreign pipeline is created after GET and before the nonce-bearing pipeline PUT, so the post-PUT GET has the request nonce/body and `created_date_millis < modified_date_millis`.  
**When:** the one permitted PUT has completed and the class-specific detector observes its asserted condition.  
**Then:** each fixture exits `4`; durable state remains exact `I[{assets-66},{target:write-issued},true]` (or the corresponding full-flow `I`) and records the issued attempt rather than promoting. The durable transaction record plus redacted durable diagnostic preserve target, transaction, nonce, detector (`created:false` or `created<modified`), and observed values; total remote mutations are exactly `1` (the PUT already issued), and a post-detection write sentinel proves **zero further remote writes**. The engine does not delete, PUT, or auto-restore either object. Manual restoration is an operator-only, documented recovery action after preserving the diagnostic evidence; a fresh run remains exit `4` until manual remediation/reconciliation.

### T-RECON-6 — all classes reject divergent unowned objects

**Source:** Sol2-#7, D2 §4.1.  
**Given:** parameterized 7 API classes (five ES classes, Kibana space, Kibana role) plus each saved-object type, with `N` or exact `I`, one target present divergent and either unstamped/foreign/malformed (ES) or any Kibana divergence.  
**When:** both callers classify it before its write boundary.  
**Then:** exit `3` if no possible mutation has been persisted, otherwise `4`; durable record is unchanged (`N`) or remains `I`; remote writes `0`; fresh run refuses until owner remediation makes it exact/deletes it.

### T-RECON-7 — final-boundary races halt and never promote

**Source:** Sol2-#1, Sol2-#7, owner ratification 5 (2026-08-04), probe classes.  
**Given:** each guarded API class and saved-object type with `I[{assets-66},{target:planned},false]`, plus pipeline and role fixtures with their unique ownership nonce. Parameterize: (a) a foreign create after pre-write GET; and (b) a visible foreign replacement after the clean post-write check but before final reverify. For the pipeline/role pre-write fixture, force the precise T-RECON-5 signatures (`created:false` for role; `created_date_millis < modified_date_millis` for pipeline).  
**When:** a transport mutation sentinel starts **before apply** and snapshots its attempt counter at detector/final-reverify failure.  
**Then:** guarded classes/saved objects in (a) exit `3`, preserve byte-identical foreign bytes, and make exactly `0` installer mutation attempts; their (b) leg exits `4`, preserves the replacement bytes, and make exactly `1` prior attempt. Pipeline/role (a) exit `4` with exact durable `I[...,{target:write-issued},true]`, one already-issued PUT, the matching durable detector evidence, and **0 further writes after detection**; they neither restore nor promote. Pipeline/role (b) exit `4`, retain the same `I`, preserve the visible replacement bytes, and make `0` writes after the final-reverify mismatch. For every fixture, the sentinel’s total attempt count and its failure snapshot prove both the whole-run attempt total and `total - snapshot = 0` post-failure writes. Every failed leg forbids promotion; manual restore remains operator-only. The qualified ES reconciliation-update race is separately recorded as an owner-ratified residual risk rather than claimed prevented.

### T-RECON-8 — read ambiguity is never absence

**Source:** Sol2-#7, D2 §4.1.  
**Given:** `N` and a parameterized malformed/timeout/5xx GET, resolve, or semantic-projection response for one class target.  
**When:** assets-only and full-flow each classify the target.  
**Then:** exit `3`; durable record remains `N`; remote writes `0`; fresh run only proceeds after a valid exact/absent classification.

## Exit contract and diagnostics

### T-EXIT-1 — persisted uncertainty always wins

**Source:** owner ratification 2, Ovs finding #6.  
**Given:** parameter cases `I[...,true]` followed by malformed record discovery, unavailable exact bundle, unresolved obligation, pre-write remote refusal, and no HTTP dispatch in the current invocation; separately, a held lock with no current enrollment mutation.  The fixture never reads a held-lock record authoritatively before acquisition.  
**When:** each case fails.  
**Then:** the persisted-uncertainty cases have engine/launcher exit `4`, retain their active record, make `0` current remote writes, and remain `4` until complete final reconciliation promotes `S`; held-lock/no-current-mutation exits `3` with no authoritative record assertion and `0` writes. Held lock after a current enrollment mutation is exclusively T-LOCK-4 and exits `4`.  
**ERRATA-4:** T-EXIT-1 controls D2 §6 lines 229, 236, and 239 and D2 §5.5/§8.2 examples: D2:229 is authoritative; all exit-3 later-rerun carve-outs are void.

### T-EXIT-2 — no persisted uncertainty preserves 2/3 distinction

**Source:** Sol2-#4.  
**Given:** parameter cases: local invalid flags before intent publication, malformed protected record with no validated persisted uncertainty, and pre-write remote conflict; no case simultaneously calls the malformed record `N`.  
**When:** each invocation fails.  
**Then:** exits are respectively `2`, `3`, and `3`; durable state is unchanged; remote writes `0`; fresh run succeeds only after input/local/remote remediation.

### T-EXIT-3 — zero-write installed verification failure is refusal, not local preflight

**Source:** Sol2 state-edge “zero-write installed rerun”.  
**Given:** `S[{assets-66}]`, no possible-mutation state, and final reverify observes one foreign divergent target before any write.  
**When:** ordinary rerun runs.  
**Then:** exit `3`; record remains `S`; remote writes `0`; fresh run refuses until target remediation.

### T-EXIT-4 — launcher preserves engine status and redacts recovery token

**Source:** Sol2-#4, D2 §6.  
**Given:** parameterized engine outcomes `2`, `3`, and `4`; for `4`, `I[...,true]` contains origin, credential-shaped strings, response body, and full UUID in test fixtures.  
**When:** `rigsignal-launcher.sh` waits for the engine.  
**Then:** launcher exit equals engine exit exactly; durable record unchanged; remote writes `0`; next run behavior equals the engine case, and output contains only `RIGSIGNAL_RECOVERY_STATE partial-remote-possible transaction=<redacted>` with none of the sensitive fixture strings.

## Flag matrix

### T-FLAG-1 — invalid/same-version version flags are local refusal

**Source:** Sol2-#1, Sol2-#6, owner ratification 2.  
**Given:** `N`, current `S`, or exact `I`, with target state parameterized absent, exact, stamped-divergent ES, unowned ES, Kibana divergent, and unreadable; flags are same-version `--upgrade`, same-version `--allow-downgrade`, both version flags, or all three flags.  
**When:** preflight evaluates flags.  
**Then:** exit `2`; durable record unchanged; **remote reads `0` and writes `0`**; fresh no-flag run follows the ordinary predicate.
**ERRATA-6:** T-FLAG-1 controls D2 §5.3 rows 206, 207, 211, and 212: every same-version version-flag combination is exit `2` before remote reads or writes; the listed create/no-op cells are void for those inputs.

### T-FLAG-2 — repair never gives Kibana rewrite authority

**Source:** OvsB, owner ratification 4, Sol2-#1.  
**Given:** separate `S[{assets-66}]`, `I[...,false]`, and `I[...,true]` cases with one present divergent Kibana saved object, space, or role under `--repair`, alone and combined with every valid transition flag.  
**When:** either caller runs.  
**Then:** `S`/`I[...,false]` exit `3` and `I[...,true]` exits `4`; each record is unchanged with exactly `0` writes; next run remains refused until the object is deleted in Kibana and rerun creates it through the guarded path.

### T-FLAG-3 — qualified ES repair/transition is the only divergent write

**Source:** Sol2-#1, Sol2-#7.  
**Given:** exact `S`/`I` with one live state parameterized exact, absent guarded-class, absent pipeline/ES-role, valid-stamped divergent ES, unowned ES, or unreadable; parameterize `--repair`, valid `--upgrade`, valid `--allow-downgrade`, `repair+upgrade`, and `repair+allow-downgrade`, with correct predecessor/direction.  
**When:** the selected predicate permits reconciliation.  
**Then:** exact exits `0`/`0`; guarded absence exits `0`/`1`; detector-negative pipeline/ES-role absence exits `0`/`1`; valid stamped divergence exits `0`/`1`; unowned/unreadable exits `3` or `4` according to `possible_mutation`, always `/0`. A pipeline/role detector-positive outcome is T-RECON-5/7 exit `4` with `I[...,write-issued,true]` and no further writes. Each permitted clean write demotes to `I` with predecessor then promotes `S`; fresh successful rows exit `0`/`0`.

### T-FLAG-4 — prior installed record does not collapse live predicates

**Source:** Sol2-#1.  
**Given:** valid prior-version `S` and one parameterized live state: absent, exact, stamped ES divergent, unowned ES divergent, or Kibana divergent.  
**When:** no flag, `--repair`, and a valid direction flag run.  
**Then:** no flag/repair exits `3` with `0` writes; valid direction yields respectively one create, zero writes, one authorized stamped-ES reconciliation, `3`/zero writes, and `3`/zero writes; durable record is `I` then current `S` only in the first three permitted cases; fresh run is a zero-write success only after permitted promotion.

## Live gate and evidence

### T-GATE-1 — class capability gate

**Source:** Ovs Q2; authoritative detector-bearing run 7 (`probe-harness/evidence/`, top-level exit 0, `DRIVER-EXIT: 0`, all class verdicts at expected status both versions, live-wire DETECTOR-* legs); run 5 = historical response-loss authority; run 6 disqualified (synthetic detectors); owner ratifications 5 and 6.  
**Given:** isolated clean 9.4.3 and 9.4.4 stacks and the release-format bundle; no installer record (`N`) per class case.  
**When:** each of seven classes is tested for absent/create, repeated conflict, divergent repeat, response loss with proven delivery, exact/divergent reread, and pre-write/update race; pipeline and role each additionally run (1) their pre-write detector race and (2) a visible post-write replacement/final-reverify halt.  
**Then:** gate test exits `0` only if every required leg of every class/version is `PASS` in the authoritative detector-bearing run (run 7, `probe-harness/evidence/`) and the top-level harness exits `0`; no nonzero class verdict is waived. Durable installer record remains `N` for capability-only legs. Absent/create=`1` successful create, exact/divergent repeat=`0`, proven-delivery response-loss=`1` attempted mutation, pre-write guarded race=`0`, post-write guarded race=`1`, and clean replay=`0` creates for each applicable guarded class. For **each** pipeline/role detector leg, the harness proves `exit=4`, retained `I[...,write-issued,true]`, durable diagnostic evidence, and `0` writes after detection: the role pre-write fixture asserts `created:false`; the pipeline pre-write fixture asserts `created_date_millis < modified_date_millis`; each class’s visible post-write replacement fixture asserts final-reverify halt with no restoration. Until the installer path lands, the harness records this as a release-format state-machine emulation and transfers engine-exit assertions to the installer unit suite. Current capability observations are assertions, not assumptions.

### T-GATE-2 — saved-object migration gate

**Source:** Sol2 probe criteria 1–8.  
**Given:** isolated 9.4.3 and 9.4.4 stacks, each five shipped saved-object types, complete reference closure, and `N`.  
**When:** literal create includes migration fields and records response projection; two conflicts preserve original bytes; a delivery-proven dropped response is resumed by a fresh process; import mapping is persisted; named migration/restart normalization is symmetric; reference graph survives; real 9.4.3→9.4.4 upgrade repeats full verification; 29 rows are deduped before replay.  
**Then:** gate exits `0` only with 18 first-run creates, `0` second-run creates, exact projections/mappings, and no unexpected physical IDs; durable installer record remains `N`; remote writes are exactly `18` then `0`; next clean replay exits `0`.

### T-GATE-3 — isolated end-to-end recovery

**Source:** D2 §8.4, owner ratification 1.  
**Given:** a unique Compose project/ports/volumes/run directory, release-format bundle, and `N`; inject crash after one saved-object verification and separately mid-dashboard member.  
**When:** a fresh process resumes each crash.  
**Then:** an injected caught exception has first engine exit `4` with protected `I[...,true]`; a real SIGKILL remains signal-derived rather than promised an engine `4`; final resume exits `0` with `S` containing 66 or 67 completed targets as caller requires; remote writes are exactly one per initially absent deduplicated identity and no more; next run is zero-write and independent semantic verification finds no unexpected IDs.
**ERRATA-7:** T-GATE-1..3 control D2 §7’s reduced-scope fallback: owner-ratified 0.3.3 scope is full ES+Kibana recovery, so a failed Kibana gate blocks release rather than authorizing an ES-only 0.3.3 implementation.

**ERRATA-8:** T-REC-4 controls D2 §3.3: `installed` records retain `caller_obligations` (implementation AMBIGUITY-1 ruling, 2026-08-04).

**ERRATA-9:** T-REC-3 controls D2 §3.3: the record schema includes an explicit `destination_map` member (Sol round-2 change 11; Kibana research destinationId persistence; implementation AMBIGUITY-2 ruling, 2026-08-04). The record's bundle version binds the bundle's actual version string, never a hardcoded release number (AMBIGUITY-3 ruling).

## Residual risks for owner sign-off

1. A same-UID/root actor can create a schema-valid record; tests only prove it gives no authority over divergent targets, not provenance detection. **Source:** D2 §2.1.
2. The narrowed lock cannot serialize friendly invocations deliberately using different canonical `XDG_STATE_HOME` domains; T-LOCK-2 documents the bypass. **Source:** owner ratification 3.
3. **OWNER-RATIFIED — detect-and-halt overwrite window (Sol addition #1, resolved as a blocker):** pipeline/role APIs still permit an unpreventable approximately-millisecond foreign-create/PUT overwrite window after GET-absent. The ratified control is detection, durable evidence, exit `4`, halt, and no auto-restore—not a claim that the write is conditional. T-RECON-5/7 and T-GATE-1 make failure to detect/refrain from further writes a release failure. **Source:** owner ratification 5 (2026-08-04).
4. **OWNER-RATIFIED — pipeline same-millisecond ambiguity:** the pipeline timestamp detector can be ambiguous when foreign creation and installer PUT share one millisecond. It is not silently reclassified as clean evidence; it remains a named limit of the ratified detector. **Source:** owner ratification 5; TIMESTAMP-PROBE addendum.
5. **OWNER-RATIFIED — write-then-restore-identical invisibility:** a foreign writer that changes then restores the identical canonical descriptor before verifier GET cannot be observed. The engine must not claim detection of that interleaving. **Source:** owner ratification 5; conditional-primitives research.
6. **OWNER-RATIFIED — qualified ES-update race (Sol addition #2, ratification 6, 2026-08-04):** a remote replacement after the ownership GET but before the reconciliation PUT can be overwritten. Ratified as a named residual: stamped-ownership GET → update PUT, `if_version` used for pipelines where a version is present, post-update re-verify recorded. Same ~ms window class as the ratification-5 residuals; strictly narrower than shipped 0.3.2 (bare upserts with no ownership GET).
7. **RESOLVED — authoritative probe gap (Sol addition #3):** run 5 resolved the index-template and Kibana-role response-loss gap; run 6 was disqualified (synthetic detector legs); **run 7 (2026-08-04, `probe-harness/evidence/`) is the authoritative detector-bearing run** — top-level exit 0, `DRIVER-EXIT: 0`, all class verdicts at expected status both versions, detector legs proven live on the wire. Engine-exit assertions remain transferred to the installer unit suite until the installer lands (that transfer is recorded in T-GATE-1, not waived).
8. **Marker-loss authority consequence (Sol addition #4):** with `N`, the remote ES stamp alone enables no-flag reconciliation. This is traceable to full-scope/self-heal policy, but deleting/selecting a different state domain must not be mistaken for an authority-preserving no-op.
9. **Version scope (Sol addition #5):** the chosen mechanisms are evidenced only on 9.4.3 and 9.4.4; other versions must fail the capability/version gate or be separately probed.
10. Remote administrators can alter an object after final GET/promotion; the tested guarantee ends at immediate full reverify under the local lock. Full ES+Kibana recovery remains blocked from release if T-GATE-1 or T-GATE-2 cannot establish a safe mechanism for every required class; no untested overwrite fallback is authorized.
